subject: BrightLane committed usage — true-up mechanics & credit handling
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.j@brightlane.com>, BrightLane RevOps <revops@brightlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightLane commit true-up — quick logistics question

Hi Sarah / RevOps team,

Thanks again for a productive renewal meeting last week. A quick operational question from our side as we prepare the Q3 billing: how would you like us to handle the upcoming true-up for the 2026 commit? Two pieces we want to confirm:

- Frequency: Would you prefer the standard quarterly true-up cadence (end of each fiscal quarter) or a single annual reconciliation?
- Make-goods / credits: If usage exceeds commit, we invoice overage; if usage is under commit, are you expecting credits applied to the following quarter or a single annual make-good?

I've attached a draft billing schedule and a short example calculation (BL_Billing_Schedule_Q2.xlsx) to make the options concrete. If easier, we can hop on a 20-min call next week to align.

Thanks,

Olga Petrov
Account Lead — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightLane commit true-up — quick logistics question

Hi Olga — thanks for the file. A few clarifying questions from RevOps before we choose cadence:

1) For quarterly true-ups, will you prorate credits within that quarter or only carry credits forward to the next quarter?
2) If we reduce a future commit during the year (we're planning a pilot that may end early), how will make-goods be handled vs. an invoice for over-usage?
3) Can you confirm whether the signed SOW has language that permits quarterly credits vs annual only? (I'm CC'ing Tom from Legal for the contract language check.)

We prefer predictable monthly cashflow, so quarterly reconciliation with credits applied promptly is ideal — but that's contingent on how you generate credits in the billing system.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Johnson
Revenue Operations Manager
BrightLane Health

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.j@brightlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, BrightLane RevOps <revops@brightlane.com>, Tom Ellis <tellis@brightlane.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightLane commit true-up — quick logistics question

Thanks Sarah — looping in Ben (sales) and Vivek (billing/finance) so we can be specific. High-level on our side:

- Quarterly true-up is supported operationally. We can create credits at quarter close and either apply them to the next invoice or issue a credit memo depending on your accounting preference.
- If you reduce a future commit mid-year, make-goods are handled as follows: any under-utilization in the prior period can be credited forward OR, if you prefer, we can invoice over-usage as it occurs and reconcile at annual true-up. The option needs to be mutually selected in the billing annex.

Ben / Vivek — can you confirm the mechanics (timing of credit memo vs applied credit) and whether Redwood can commit to issuing a credit memo within 30 days of quarter close if BrightLane requests it? Also marking this for Tom for contract check on language.

Olga

On a separate note, attaching the signed SOW we have on file for reference (Signed_SOW-BrightLane.pdf).

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sarah Johnson <sarah.j@brightlane.com>, BrightLane RevOps <revops@brightlane.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightLane commit true-up — quick logistics question

Quick note from Finance on the operational choices:

Option A — Quarterly credits applied to next invoice (recommended for cashflow predictability):
- At quarter close we calculate actual usage vs committed token bands.
- If usage < commit, we create a credit memo equal to (commit - actual) * committed rate.
- Credit memos can be applied to the next invoice automatically if BrightLane elects that option; otherwise we can post a standalone credit on your account.
- Timeframe: credit memo generated within 30 days of quarter close; application on next invoice.

Option B — Annual reconciliation with single make-good/true-up:
- We aggregate usage across the year, invoice net overage or issue credit at year-end.
- Simpler contract language but less frequent cashflow correction.

Important caveats: credits are financial instruments and cannot be refunded as cash without a special request; refunds (cash) require legal sign-off and a short finance review. Also, if you lower a future commit mid-year, we will prorate commit bands for subsequent quarters but make-goods for past quarters are settled as described above.

Ben — any commercial constraints to call out (discount stacking, prior credits)?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Billing & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Ellis <tellis@brightlane.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, BrightLane RevOps <revops@brightlane.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightLane commit true-up — quick logistics question

Olga / Vivek — I reviewed the SOW. Two contractual points to flag: 

1) The current SOW references an "annual true-up" clause under Section 4.2. We can accept quarterly operational reconciliation but need an amendment to the SOW to make it explicit (doesn't have to be complex; an addendum linking to the billing annex will suffice).
2) The SOW does not currently define make-goods as a credit vs. refund; to avoid ambiguity, provide language that makes credits the default, with refunds only by written request and subject to Redwood's refund policy.

If you can send a short addendum with the option selected (quarterly with credits applied to next invoice, credit memos issued within 30 days), we can review and sign quickly.

Tom Ellis
General Counsel
BrightLane Health

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tellis@brightlane.com>, Sarah Johnson <sarah.j@brightlane.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightLane commit true-up — quick logistics question

Tom / Sarah — thanks for the clear direction. Summary and next steps (agreed):

- Cadence: Quarterly true-ups (end of each fiscal quarter).
- Credits: Redwood will generate credit memos for under-utilization within 30 days of quarter close. Credits will be applied to the next invoice by default. Refunds (cash) are available only by written request and subject to Redwood's finance policy.
- Commit reductions: If BrightLane reduces a future commit mid-year, we will prorate forward commits for subsequent quarters; prior-quarter make-goods remain subject to the reconciliation described above.
- Contract: Redwood to send a one-page SOW addendum reflecting the quarterly-credit option and the 30-day credit-memo SLA. Once signed, we will operationalize the workflow with billing.

Action items:
- Ben: draft SOW addendum and share for legal review (target: 2026-07-20).
- Vivek: prepare billing config to auto-apply credit memos to next invoice and confirm any ERP constraints (target: 2026-07-22).
- Sarah / Tom: confirm acceptance of the addendum after Ben shares.

I'll put the draft addendum in the HubSpot deal and share the link when ready. Thanks all — happy to set a 20-min sync if anyone prefers to talk through edge cases.

Olga Petrov
Account Lead — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
